input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The shape check before Editor.edit_files tests only for os.PathLike and no longer wraps a plain str, so a string filename is passed on as an iterable and consumed character by character when building the editor command.
- failure path: click.edit(filename="notes.txt") launches the editor with the nine single-character files n, o, t, e, s, ., t, x, t instead of notes.txt; saving creates stray files in the working directory and the intended file is never opened.

Reviewer finding
- description: The new check stops wrapping string filenames in a single-element tuple. Include `str` alongside `os.PathLike` to preserve existing string filename support.
- rationale: Calling `click.edit(filename="notes.txt")` now passes the string directly to `edit_files`, which accepts an iterable of filenames. The string is therefore processed as individual characters, causing the editor to open character-named files instead of the requested file.
critique: The finding states the same mechanism as the label. The isinstance check no longer wraps str, so a string filename reaches edit_files as an iterable and is iterated character by character, which opens character-named files instead of notes.txt.
